judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 4 Indicators in Strand 2 Algebra, Sub-strand 'Unknowns, Expressions and Equations' (same statement-type grain, same coordinate rank 0). B4.2.2.1.2 asks learners to translate a pictorial or concrete representation into a symbolic equation, establishing the meaning of the symbolic form and of the symbol standing for an unknown (parent Content Standard B4.2.2.1: express a given problem as an equation with a symbol for an unknown). B4.2.2.2.7 reverses and extends that translation: learners must read a given equation with one unknown and generate a matching problem situation (parent Content Standard B4.2.2.2: solve one-step equations involving a symbol for an unknown). Facility in mapping concrete/pictorial situations onto symbolic equations substantively supports the more demanding inverse task of inventing a valid contextual problem for a given symbolic equation, so a same-rank forward direction from the representation-to-symbol skill to the equation-to-problem skill is supported by the statement text and LC tags ('equation', 'representation', 'symbolic form' vs 'equation', 'unknown', 'problem'). Confidence is moderated because both endpoints carry upstream audit/merge context and their source evidence excerpts are truncated (24 omitted evidence items each), and the shared lexical/code-prefix signals alone would not establish direction.

judgment.rationale: Same-grain Indicator pair, both BASIC 6 (rank 2, gap 0) under Strand 1: Number / Sub-Strand 2: Number Operations. First (B6.1.2.2.1) is efficient multiplication of multi-digit numbers by 2- or 3-digit numbers under content standard B6.1.2.2; second (B6.1.2.4.1) is efficient division of 3-digit numbers by a 1-digit number under content standard B6.1.2.4. These are complementary inverse whole-number operations taught in the same sub-strand and grade, both framed as efficient computational procedures, giving substantive conceptual and skill coherence beyond the generic token overlap ('digit', 'numbers', 'efficiently') and shared ancestry that triggered nomination. No directed dependency is supported: division by a single-digit divisor relies on basic multiplication facts and subtraction rather than on the more complex multi-digit-by-2/3-digit multiplication procedure, and there is no evidence of the reverse dependency either, so same-rank buildsTowards in either direction is not justified. Canonical relatesTo with null direction. Evidence limitation: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and all endpoints/ancestors carry upstream audit/merge/code context, which was retained rather than resolved.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are BASIC 5 Indicators (same rank 1) within Strand 4: Data, Sub-Strand 1 'Data Collection, Organisation, Presentation, Interpretation and Analysis', but under different Content Standards: B5.4.1.1 'Differentiate between first-hand and second-hand data' (ef319b94 = 'Explain the difference between first-hand and second-hand data.') and B5.4.1.2 'Construct and interpret double bar graphs to draw conclusions' (9a90f500 = 'Identify examples of double bar graphs used in a variety of print and electronic media...'). There is genuine pair-specific coherence: graphs located in newspapers, magazines and the internet are precisely the media-sourced (second-hand) data the other indicator asks pupils to characterise, so the two reinforce each other about data sources and their published representations. However, the evidence does not establish that proficiency in either is substantively needed for or developmentally supports the other — one concerns defining data provenance, the other recognising a specific graph type in media — and the shared BASIC 5 rank means same-rank direction would need stronger evidence than the weak lexical/code-prefix signals ('data', 'and', 'the', shared b5.4.1 segments) supplied. Symmetric relatesTo is the supported judgment.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 5 Indicators (same grain, same rank 1) under the same Content Standard B5.1.4.1 on decimal fractions. B5.1.4.1.1 establishes describing and representing decimals up to the thousandths concretely, pictorially and symbolically and relating them to fractions; B5.1.4.1.2 requires comparing and ordering decimal fractions and mixed common/decimal fractions to the thousandths using <, >, =. Same-rank direction is justified by substantive statement evidence rather than code order alone: secure representation and fraction-decimal equivalence at thousandths place value is the understanding that comparison and ordering operate on, and the mixed common/decimal comparison task presupposes the relating-to-fractions work of the first. Shared parent and code prefix were not treated as sufficient on their own; hierarchy is caveated because both endpoints and the parent carry unresolved-ancestry/framework-root fallback and truncated source evidence, so the judgment rests on the visible statement texts and resolved BASIC 5 grade coordinates.

B4.3.3.2.2 (LCs: 'Select referents for the units cm² or m²', 'Justify referents for the units cm² or m²') develops benchmark sense for square units; B4.3.3.2.5 (LC: construct different rectangles for a given area in cm2 or m2 to show many rectangles may share the same area) develops construction and area-conservation reasoning. These are substantively coherent, complementary square-unit/area skills that reinforce one another instructionally, but the bounded evidence shows no pair-specific developmental dependency: nothing in .5 calls on referents, estimation, or benchmarks, and the only directional signals available (source code order, page gap 1, shared ancestry, cm2/m2 token and trigram overlap, shared LC tag 'area') are not positive semantic evidence and cannot license same-rank buildsTowards in either direction. Symmetric relatesTo is therefore the supported judgment in canonical endpoint order with null direction. Limitations: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and all endpoints/ancestors carry upstream audit/merge/code context retained below.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 5 Indicators (same grain, resolved coordinate rank 1) under the same Algebra / Patterns and Relationships Content Standard B5.2.1.1 'Determine the pattern rule to make predictions about subsequent elements.' The second SFI (B5.2.1.1.1) has learners extend a given pattern with and without concrete materials and explain how each element differs from the preceding one — i.e. articulating the element-to-element rule with concrete support (LCs: 'extend a given pattern with and without concrete materials'; 'explain how each element of a pattern differs from the preceding one'). The first SFI (B5.2.1.1.3) requires predicting subsequent elements in a given pattern, which applies that identified rule forward without concrete scaffolding. Proficiency in extending and verbalising the difference between successive elements substantively supports success in predicting later elements, giving a same-rank developmental direction from second to first; the .1/.3 code sequence is only weak corroboration and was not treated as decisive. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each), so this rests on the visible statement text and LCs.
